conventions.convention: Hellinger distance is the root-L2 quantity h(P,Q) = (∫(√p−√q)² dμ)^(1/2), without a normalization factor, using supplied finite-valued densities against a common sigma-finite measure.
Library total variation is sup_A |P(A)−Q(A)|; consequently density L1 distance equals twice total variation.
KL support uses the direction D(P0||Pθ) and requires positive prior mass on a measurable subset of each strict KL neighborhood.

The consistency theorem assumes a proper prior, well-specified IID truth, an explicitly supplied jointly measurable normalized density, and measurable strict complements Vη = {θ:d(Pθ,P0)>η}. Separate density representatives do not supply joint measurability.

Posterior likelihood normalization is used only on finite-positive evidence fibers; the prior itself fills all other fibers. Testing error series start at n=1, and the conclusion is almost-sure consistency.
AC is explicitly assumed through the imported general density and KL conventions; the finite and countable witnesses supply their densities directly.
The inconsistency witness uses the discrete metric on model laws, not Hellinger or total variation; its prior masses are Π({0})=0 and Π({k})=2^(−k) for k≥1.

load_bearing.statement: For a proper-prior, well-specified dominated IID model with a supplied jointly measurable normalized density and KL support, summable type-I errors and summable uniform type-II errors on each nonempty measurable metric-separated complement imply Π_n(Vη|X_{1:n})→0 almost surely for every fixed η>0. Every Hellinger ball about P0 is measurable and has positive prior mass, and h(P0,Pθ)^4≤2D(P0||Pθ).

Assuming AC for the imported density-representative convention, root-L2 Hellinger distance for probability laws with a specified common sigma-finite dominator is independent of the common dominating measure, and TV(P,Q)≤h(P,Q), h(P,Q)²≤2TV(P,Q), where TV is the event supremum.
For supplied finite-valued nonnegative measurable density representatives p and q of probability laws against a specified common sigma-finite positive measure μ, h(P,Q):=(∫(√p−√q)² dμ)^(1/2).

An injective parameter-to-law mapping and positive prior mass in every KL neighborhood of a well-specified dominated IID truth do not suffice for posterior consistency in every metric on model laws without uniform testability.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page, evidence-normalizer definition, and finite-positive scaling proposition. The consistency theorem supplies a proper prior and jointly measurable normalized density, uses the published dominated-kernel Bayes formula with prior filling, and independently proves eventual finite-positive evidence under P0. It does not infer joint measurability or P0-valid fibers merely from prior-predictive almost-everywhere validity.

Checked the contraction page and its Hellinger definition, comparison lemma, denominator lemma, testing lemma, and contraction theorem statements. Root-L2 Hellinger, full density L1 = 2TV, directional KL, proper-prior normalization, and supplied joint density conventions agree. The contraction page proves its own quantitative result and asserts convergence in probability only; it does not import an almost-sure rate from this batch's consistency theorem.
